battery: ~30 h ANC on, 3-min charge = 3 h, USB-C
best: The all-round ANC benchmark: best-in-class noise cancelling, foldable, great app EQ.
extra: No aptX. Spatial is app-driven, not baked in. Plastic build.

standalone.note: Full audio + ANC work app-free; Sound Connect is only for EQ / spatial / firmware.

name: Sony WH-1000XM5
spatial: 360 Reality Audio via app; no head tracking
micNote: Four beamforming mics; solid call clarity — the XM6 improved on this.
battery: ~30 h ANC on, 3-min = 3 h, USB-C
best: Still excellent and often ~$300; near-XM6 sound and ANC, doesn't fold flat.
extra: Non-folding design. Superseded by the XM6.

standalone.note: Works fully without the app; app adds EQ and 360 Reality Audio.

name: Bose QuietComfort Ultra Headphones (2nd gen)
bt: BT 5.3 · Snapdragon Sound / aptX Adaptive · multipoint
spatial: Bose Immersive Audio (Still / Motion) — Bose's own head-tracked spatialiser
soft: Bose app (iOS / Android) — EQ, ANC modes, Immersive Audio toggle
micNote: Good voice pickup and wind handling; typical premium-ANC call quality.
battery: ~24 h (18 h with Immersive Audio), USB-C
best: The most effective ANC + the comfiest fit; Immersive Audio needs no app-side content.
extra: Immersive Audio costs ~6 h battery. 2nd gen adds USB-C lossless; 1st gen doesn't.

standalone.note: ANC + audio work out of the box; Bose app for EQ, modes and Immersive Audio.

name: Sennheiser Momentum 4 Wireless
bt: BT 5.2 · aptX Adaptive / aptX / AAC · multipoint
spatial: None (no spatial-audio mode)
soft: Sennheiser Smart Control (iOS / Android) — parametric EQ, sound zones
micNote: Below-average call mic for the class — muffled outdoors. Music playback is the strength.
battery: ~60 h ANC on — class-leading, USB-C
best: Best battery in the category by far, and warm detailed sound; frequently ~$250.
extra: No spatial audio. Weak call mic. Plain design.

standalone.note: Plays and cancels noise app-free; Smart Control only for parametric EQ.

name: Bowers & Wilkins Px7 S2e
bt: BT 5.2 · aptX Adaptive / aptX HD · multipoint
spatial: None on-device; works as a normal stereo pair with platform spatialisers
soft: B&W Music app (iOS / Android) — EQ, ANC
micNote: Functional for calls, nothing special. This is a music-first headphone.
battery: ~30 h ANC on, USB-C
best: Best pure sound quality of the mainstream ANC set; premium materials.
extra: ANC trails Sony/Bose. No spatial. App is basic.

standalone.note: Standalone; app is optional EQ + ANC tuning.

name: Beats Studio Pro
bt: BT 5.3 · Apple H-class + Android fast-pair (dual chip)
wired: 3.5 mm analog, USB-C audio — lossless via USB-C
spatial: Spatial Audio with dynamic head tracking (works on iOS AND Android)
soft: None dedicated — iOS Settings / Android Beats app
micNote: Decent voice pickup; the USB-C connection also carries a clean mic path for calls.
battery: ~24 h ANC (40 h ANC off), fast charge, USB-C
best: Spatial Audio + USB-C lossless that work cross-platform; often ~$170 on sale.
extra: Middling ANC, tight clamp, no folding hinge. Bass-forward sound.

standalone.note: No dedicated app needed on either platform; Spatial Audio is a system toggle.

name: Sonos Ace
w24: None (BT only; Wi-Fi link to a Sonos soundbar)
wired: USB-C audio (lossless), 3.5 mm via USB-C adapter
spatial: Dolby Atmos with head tracking + TV Audio Swap from a Sonos Arc/Beam soundbar
soft: Sonos app (iOS / Android) — EQ, ANC, TV swap, spatial toggle
micNote: Solid call mics; the headline feature is pulling TV audio off a Sonos soundbar, not the mic.
battery: ~30 h ANC on, 3-min = 3 h, USB-C
best: Best-in-class if you own a Sonos soundbar — instant private Atmos TV audio. Great build.
extra: TV Swap needs a Sonos Arc/Beam. Not part of multiroom Sonos. App required for most features.

standalone.note: Basic listening works app-free, but ANC modes, EQ and TV Audio Swap all need the Sonos app.

name: Nothing Headphone (1)
spatial: Spatial audio with head tracking; Sound by KEF tuning
soft: Nothing X (iOS / Android) — 8-band EQ, ANC, controls
micNote: Six mics, clear enough for calls. Distinctive transparent industrial design.
battery: ~35 h ANC on (80 h off), USB-C
best: Most features per dollar in the ANC class — LDAC, 3.5 mm, spatial, big battery, ~$270.
extra: ANC a step behind Sony/Bose. Bulky. Brand-new — long-term support unproven.

standalone.note: Audio + ANC work app-free; Nothing X only for EQ and controls.

name: Sony WF-1000XM6
spatial: 360 Reality Audio via app; head tracking with supported content
micType: Beamforming call mics + bone-conduction voice sensor, AI noise reduction
micNote: Reviewers call call quality the biggest XM5→XM6 upgrade; voice stays clear in wind and street noise.
battery: ~8 h ANC on, case adds ~16 h, USB-C + Qi
best: Best all-round flagship ANC earbuds of 2026 — top-tier noise cancelling with natural, detailed sound.
extra: Launched Feb 2026 at $330; case is bulkier than XM5 and only three eartip sizes ship in the box.

standalone.note: Full audio + ANC work app-free; app only for EQ, 360RA and firmware.

name: Bose QuietComfort Ultra Earbuds (2nd Gen)
bt: BT 5.4 · aptX Adaptive / SBC / AAC · multipoint (2 devices)
spatial: Bose Immersive Audio (Still / Motion modes, head tracking)
micType: Multi-mic beamforming array with AI noise suppression
micNote: Call quality was the main 2nd-gen improvement; still slightly behind Sony/Apple in wind.
battery: ~6 h ANC on, case adds ~18 h (24 h total), USB-C + Qi (new for gen 2)
best: The strongest ANC in any earbud plus the best Immersive Audio implementation; ideal for flights and commutes.
extra: Battery life did not improve over gen 1 (6 h) and lags Sony/Apple; Bose still lacks LDAC and stereo mic recording.

standalone.note: ANC, Aware and Immersive Audio toggle from the buds; app needed only for EQ and mode customization.

name: Samsung Galaxy Buds4 Pro
bt: BT 5.4 · SSC UHQ 24-bit/96k (Galaxy only) / AAC / SBC · Auracast · auto-switch between Galaxy devices
spatial: 360 Audio with head tracking (Galaxy devices only)
soft: Galaxy Wearable app (Android only; no iOS app)
micType: Beamforming mic array + voice pickup unit
micNote: Clear voice in quiet rooms; Galaxy AI live-translate features are the headline, not raw call quality.
battery: ~6 h ANC on (up to 26 h with case), USB-C + Qi
best: The obvious pick for Galaxy phone owners — 2-way drivers, adaptive ANC and deep One UI integration.
extra: Launched Mar 2026; hi-res codec, 360 Audio and most AI features require a Samsung phone, and there is no iOS app at all.

standalone.note: Audio + ANC work on any BT device; EQ, firmware and AI features need Galaxy Wearable on Android.

name: Google Pixel Buds Pro 2
bt: BT 5.4 · AAC / SBC · LE Audio · multipoint (2 devices) · Fast Pair
spatial: Spatial Audio with head tracking (Pixel phones only)
soft: Pixel Buds app (Android; settings built into Pixel phones)
micType: 3-mic array per bud with wind-noise reduction + Clear Calling
micNote: Solid, natural voice on calls; Gemini hands-free conversation is the differentiator.
battery: ~8 h ANC on (12 h off), case adds to ~30 h, USB-C + Qi
best: The best small, light ANC buds for Android/Pixel users, with Gemini and excellent multipoint.
extra: Regularly discounted to $169–179; head-tracked spatial audio and some features are Pixel-only, and there is no iOS app.

standalone.note: Works app-free on any device; EQ and firmware via the Pixel Buds app on Android.

name: Nothing Ear (3)
bt: BT 5.4 · LDAC / AAC / SBC · multipoint (2 devices)
spatial: None
micType: In-bud mic array plus 'Super Mic' dual mics built into the charging case (hold case to mouth)
micNote: Bud mics are average-to-good; the case Super Mic is clearer in noise but reviewers call it a gimmick in practice.
battery: ~5.5 h ANC on (8.5 h off), case to ~37 h, USB-C + Qi
best: Stylish metal-case buds with big, tunable sound and LDAC at a mid-range price.
extra: Fourth-gen Nothing Ear (Sept 2025); ANC-on battery is short and the $30 premium over Ear (2024) buys mostly looks and the case mic.

standalone.note: Audio + ANC work without the app; Nothing X needed for EQ, ChatGPT pinch and Super Mic settings.

name: Jabra Elite 10 Gen 2
bt: BT 5.3 · AAC / SBC · LE Audio · multipoint (2 devices) · case doubles as LE Audio transmitter via USB-C / 3.5 mm
wired: Case only: USB-C / 3.5 mm input to the LE Audio smart case (buds still wireless)
spatial: Dolby Atmos spatial sound with head tracking
micNote: Jabra's call heritage shows — one of the clearest consumer buds for voice, even outdoors.
battery: ~6 h ANC on (8 h off), case to ~27 h, USB-C + Qi
best: Semi-open comfortable fit and a case that streams from in-flight / TV 3.5 mm jacks — a traveller's pick.
extra: Jabra exited consumer earbuds in 2024; Gen 2 still gets firmware (Jan 2026) but stock is intermittent and heavily discounted.

standalone.note: All audio, ANC and case-transmitter features work app-free; Sound+ for EQ and firmware.

name: Sennheiser Momentum True Wireless 4
bt: BT 5.4 · aptX Lossless / aptX Adaptive / AAC / SBC · LE Audio / Auracast · multipoint (2 devices)
spatial: None
micNote: Adequate call quality but struggles more than Jabra/Sony in wind and traffic.
battery: ~7.5 h ANC on, case to ~30 h, USB-C + Qi
best: Best-sounding mainstream ANC bud for audiophiles, with aptX Lossless on Snapdragon Sound phones.
extra: ANC is a tier below Bose/Sony; bulky bud shape does not suit small ears, and street price has fallen to ~$200.

standalone.note: Audio + ANC app-free; Smart Control needed for EQ, Sound Zones and codec choice.

name: Beats Powerbeats Pro 2
bt: BT 5.3 · AAC / SBC · Apple H2 chip · one-touch pairing on iOS and Android · audio sharing
spatial: Personalized Spatial Audio with head tracking (Apple devices)
soft: Built into iOS; Beats app on Android
micNote: Effectively AirPods Pro 2 call quality with a hook; excellent voice isolation.
battery: ~8 h ANC on (10 h off), case to ~45 h, USB-C + Qi
best: Ear-hook workout buds with real ANC, heart-rate sensing and H2-class ANC/transparency.
extra: Case is huge; hook fit fights glasses arms and ANC is a notch below AirPods Pro 3 because of the vented design.

standalone.note: Everything works app-free on iOS; Android needs the Beats app for firmware and Find My Device.

name: Technics EAH-AZ100
bt: BT 5.3 · LDAC / LC3 / AAC / SBC · multipoint (3 devices) · Auracast
spatial: Dolby Atmos with head tracking
micType: Multi-mic array with Voice Focus AI noise suppression
micNote: Voice Focus AI makes these among the best call buds tested; voice stays intelligible in heavy noise.
battery: ~10 h ANC on (12 h off), case to ~28 h, USB-C + Qi
best: Audiophile-grade 'magnetic fluid' drivers with 3-device multipoint and long battery — the Android hi-fi pick.
extra: ANC is good rather than class-leading; three-device multipoint disables LDAC.

standalone.note: Audio + ANC work app-free; app for EQ, multipoint config and firmware.

name: Apple AirPods 4 (ANC)
bt: BT 5.3 · AAC / SBC · Apple H2 chip · auto-switch across Apple devices
spatial: Personalized Spatial Audio with head tracking (Apple devices)
soft: Built into iOS/macOS; no Android app
micType: Beamforming mics + voice accelerometer (H2), Voice Isolation
micNote: Apple's H2 voice processing gives very clear calls despite the open, tip-less fit.
battery: ~4 h ANC on (5 h off), case to ~20 h ANC, USB-C + Qi (no MagSafe)
best: The only tip-less open-fit bud with real ANC — for people who hate silicone tips but want some isolation.
extra: No ear tips means ANC and bass depend heavily on your ear shape; ANC-on battery is only ~4 h and Android gets basic BT audio only.

standalone.note: Full function on Apple devices with no app; on Android it is a plain BT headset without ANC controls.

name: OnePlus Buds Pro 3
bt: BT 5.4 · LHDC 5.0 / AAC / SBC · multipoint (2 devices) · Google Fast Pair
spatial: OnePlus 3D Audio with head tracking (OnePlus/OPPO phones)
soft: HeyMelody (iOS / Android); built in on OnePlus phones
micType: 3-mic array per bud with AI call noise reduction
micNote: Fine indoors; voice gets processed and thin in wind or traffic.
battery: ~6 h ANC on (10 h off), case to ~43 h, USB-C + Qi
best: Dynaudio-tuned dual-driver buds with strong ANC and hi-res LHDC for well under $150.
extra: LHDC only helps on OnePlus/OPPO phones; often on sale to $129 as the Buds Pro 4 rolls out in some markets.

standalone.note: Audio + ANC work app-free; HeyMelody for EQ, gestures and firmware.

name: SteelSeries Arctis GameBuds
w24: USB-C 2.4 GHz dongle (PC / PS5 / Switch / Meta Quest; Xbox version sold separately)
bt: BT 5.3 · AAC / SBC · one-tap switch between dongle and BT (not simultaneous)
spatial: None (uses platform 3D audio such as PS5 Tempest / Windows Sonic)
soft: Arctis companion app (iOS / Android) · SteelSeries GG on PC
micType: Dual mics per bud with AI noise cancellation
micNote: Best-in-class for gaming earbuds — teammates hear you clearly, though not boom-mic clean.
battery: ~10 h per charge (ANC on, 2.4 GHz), case to ~40 h, USB-C + Qi
best: The best gaming earbuds tested — low-latency dongle, real ANC, IP55, and 100+ game EQ presets.
extra: Xbox needs the separate Xbox SKU; you cannot run 2.4 GHz game audio and phone BT at the same time.

standalone.note: Plug the dongle in and play; app only for EQ, ANC tuning and firmware.

name: Sony INZONE Buds
w24: USB-C 2.4 GHz dongle (PC / PS5; no Xbox)
bt: BT 5.3 LE Audio only (LC3) — phone must support LE Audio
spatial: 360 Spatial Sound for Gaming (PC via INZONE Hub); PS5 Tempest 3D
micType: Dual mic per bud + AI noise reduction
micNote: Clear voice chat on PC/PS5; slightly compressed compared to the GameBuds.
battery: ~12 h ANC on via 2.4 GHz, case adds ~12 h (24 h total), USB-C only
best: Longest per-charge battery of any gaming bud, with XM-grade ANC and PS5-native features.
extra: Bluetooth is LE Audio only, so many phones and all Macs cannot pair over BT; no Qi charging.

standalone.note: 2.4 GHz works out of the box; INZONE Hub for EQ, spatial and sidetone.

name: Razer Hammerhead V3 HyperSpeed
w24: USB-C HyperSpeed 2.4 GHz dongle (PC / PS5 / Switch / mobile)
bt: BT 5.3 · AAC / SBC · switch between dongle and BT
spatial: THX Spatial Audio (PC via Razer Synapse)
soft: Razer Audio app (iOS / Android) · Synapse on PC
micType: Dual mics per bud with noise cancellation
micNote: Usable for voice chat but thinner and noisier than SteelSeries or Sony.
battery: ~7 h ANC on over 2.4 GHz, case to ~30 h, USB-C + Qi
best: Razer-branded low-latency buds with Chroma case lighting and THX spatial for PC players.
extra: Replaced the Hammerhead Pro HyperSpeed in 2025; ANC and mic trail the GameBuds and battery is middling.

standalone.note: Dongle audio works app-free; Razer Audio app for EQ, ANC and firmware.

name: Sony PlayStation Pulse Explore
w24: PlayStation Link USB adapter (PS5 / PC / Mac); PS Portal has Link built in
bt: BT 5.3 · SBC / AAC · can run BT phone audio alongside PS Link
spatial: PS5 Tempest 3D AudioTech
soft: None — settings live in PS5 system menus
micType: Dual mics per bud with AI noise rejection
micNote: Sony's AI noise rejection gives clean party chat; no ANC on the listening side.
battery: ~5 h per charge, case adds ~10 h (15 h total), USB-C
best: The only earbuds with lossless PlayStation Link and native PS Portal support.
extra: No ANC, short battery, and the planar drivers' bass is light; fit is loose for many ears.

standalone.note: PS Link works instantly on PS5/Portal; there is no app at all.

name: HyperX Cloud Mix Buds 2
w24: USB-C 2.4 GHz dongle (PC / PS5 / Switch / Android)
bt: BT 5.3 · AAC / SBC · switch between dongle and BT
spatial: DTS Headphone:X spatial (PC via NGENUITY)
micType: Dual mic per bud with noise reduction
micNote: Adequate for chat; muffled outdoors and behind the GameBuds.
battery: ~10 h ANC off (2.4 GHz), case to ~35 h, USB-C
best: Budget dongle buds with strong battery life for PC and PS5 players.
extra: ANC is mild; mobile app support is thin and the dongle has no Xbox mode.

standalone.note: Dongle audio works without software; NGENUITY for EQ and DTS.

name: Shokz OpenRun Pro 2
spatial: None
micType: Dual noise-cancelling mics on the band
micNote: Clear enough for calls on a run; wind noise is the main enemy.
battery: ~12 h music, USB-C (first Shokz Run model without the magnetic pogo cable)
best: The best bone-conduction headphones — DualPitch bone + air drivers add real bass while ears stay fully open for traffic awareness.
extra: Open design leaks sound at high volume and is drowned out on noisy streets; IP55 only, not for swimming.

standalone.note: Fully functional without the app; app adds EQ presets and firmware.

name: Shokz OpenSwim Pro
bt: BT 5.4 · SBC · multipoint (2 devices) · 32 GB onboard MP3 player for swimming
spatial: None
micType: Dual mics on the band (calls in BT mode only)
micNote: Calls are fine on land; the mic is a secondary feature on a swim-first product.
battery: ~9 h Bluetooth or ~6 h MP3 mode, magnetic pogo cable
best: IP68 bone-conduction set for swimmers — load MP3s and go, then use Bluetooth on dry land.
extra: Bluetooth does not work underwater; sound quality is a step below OpenRun Pro 2 and it uses Shokz's proprietary charger.

standalone.note: MP3 and BT modes work with no app; app for EQ and firmware only.

name: Shokz OpenFit 2
spatial: None
micType: 4-mic array with AI call noise reduction
micNote: Better call pickup than Shokz's bone-conduction bands; still wind-sensitive.
battery: ~11 h per charge, case to ~48 h, USB-C
best: Air-conduction hook buds that sound markedly better than bone conduction while keeping the ear canal open for awareness.
extra: Open-ear leakage is audible to neighbours at moderate volume; hooks fight glasses arms and there is no ANC by design.

standalone.note: Full function without the app; app for EQ, button mapping and firmware.

name: Shokz OpenMeet UC
form: Bone conduction · open-ear (office headset w/ boom)
w24: USB-C Loop 120 Bluetooth dongle (UC version) for PC / Mac
bt: BT 5.4 · SBC · multipoint (2 devices) · Teams / Zoom certified
spatial: None
micType: Flexible boom mic with dual noise-cancelling mics
micNote: Boom-mic voice rivals dedicated office headsets — colleagues hear you clearly with background noise stripped out.
battery: ~15 h music / ~14 h talk, magnetic pogo cable, 5-min charge = 2 h
best: All-day open-ear office headset — bone conduction over the head, ears free for the room, best mic in the open-ear class.
extra: Niche: music quality is bone-conduction thin and leaks; the over-head band and boom look unusual and the charger is proprietary.

standalone.note: Dongle and BT work plug-and-play; desktop app only for firmware and mic tuning.

name: Suunto Wing
bt: BT 5.2 · SBC · multipoint (2 devices) · head-gesture controls
spatial: None
micNote: Serviceable for a quick call mid-run; not a calling headset.
battery: ~10 h per charge, included power-bank clip adds ~20 h, magnetic pogo cable
best: Bone-conduction set for night runners — built-in LED safety lights plus a portable charging dock.
extra: Sound is behind OpenRun Pro 2, it uses a proprietary charger, and Suunto's headphone line has thin US retail presence.

standalone.note: Works with no app; Suunto app for firmware and EQ.

name: Bose Ultra Open Earbuds
bt: BT 5.3 · aptX Adaptive / AAC / SBC · multipoint (2 devices)
spatial: Bose Immersive Audio with head tracking
micNote: Calls are clear in quiet spaces but degrade quickly outdoors and in wind.
battery: ~7 h (4.5 h with Immersive Audio), case to ~27 h, USB-C (Qi via optional cover)
best: Cuff-style clip-ons with the best sound of any open-ear bud — the pick for wearing all day around people.
extra: Expensive for what is essentially open-ear; leaks sound at high volume, no ANC, and Immersive Audio halves battery.

standalone.note: Audio and modes work without the app; Bose app for EQ and Immersive Audio settings.

name: Sony LinkBuds Open
spatial: 360 Reality Audio via app (Sony apps)
micType: Dual mics per bud + AI noise reduction
micNote: Sony's noise reduction keeps voice clear even with the open ring design.
battery: ~8 h per charge, case to ~22 h, USB-C
best: Sony's ring-driver open bud with Auto Volume and Wide Area Tap — everyday awareness buds with good voice quality.
extra: Ring fit is fiddly and can loosen during exercise; open design leaks and offers no isolation on transit.

standalone.note: Works app-free; Sound Connect for EQ, Auto Volume and firmware.

name: Anker Soundcore AeroFit 2
bt: BT 5.4 · LDAC / AAC / SBC · multipoint (2 devices) · Auracast
spatial: None
micNote: Fine for quick calls indoors; struggles with wind on a run.
battery: ~10 h per charge, case to ~42 h, USB-C
best: Budget open-ear hook buds with LDAC and adjustable hooks — the value pick for awareness during workouts.
extra: Bass-light and leaky like all open-ear buds; hooks are bulkier than Shokz OpenFit 2.

standalone.note: Works app-free; Soundcore app for EQ and hook-angle tips.

name: SteelSeries Arctis Nova Elite
w24: GameHub base station (Hi-Res 96 kHz/24-bit over 2.4 GHz) + USB-C dongle
bt: BT 5.3 · LC3+ · multipoint; OmniPlay mixes up to 4 sources (PC + 2 consoles + BT) at once
wired: Via GameHub: 3× USB-C, optical in, 3.5 mm line-in/out
spatial: First Hi-Res Wireless certified headset · on-device virtual 7.1 · 360° Spatial Audio · full Sonar suite on PC
soft: SteelSeries GG + Sonar (Windows only for Sonar)
micNote: Dual mics — the ClearCast retractable boom plus a smart-switching on-ear beamforming mic; Sonar AI processing on PC. Among the most flexible mic setups on a gaming headset.
battery: 2× 700 mAh (~30 h each), hot-swap in the GameHub — effectively unlimited
best: SteelSeries' no-limits flagship: first Hi-Res Wireless certified headset, ~42% stronger ANC than rivals, all-metal build, and the GameHub mixes a PC + two consoles + Bluetooth simultaneously.
extra: $600. GameHub-dependent, so not portable. Sonar is still Windows-only. Overkill for anyone not chasing wireless hi-res.

standalone.note: Full audio + virtual 7.1 + hi-res from the GameHub; Sonar app is optional tuning. The GameHub is required.

software.name: SteelSeries GG + Sonar
software.windows: Full: SteelSeries GG + Sonar — parametric EQ, virtual 7.1 / 360 Spatial, AI noise-cancel mic, ChatMix.
software.macos: GG runs, but Sonar (EQ, spatial, AI mic) is Windows-only — Mac gets device settings + firmware only.
software.linux: No app. Generic USB audio; on the Nova Pro the base station still does 7.1 + source-switch in hardware.
software.console: No app — on-headset controls plus the console's own EQ. Nova Pro base station ChatMix dial still works.
